stem.text: A guitar string vibrates to create a sound. The speed of the wave in the guitar string is always $440\,\text{m s}^{-1}$. The vibrating string creates a sound wave that moves in the air with a speed of $330\,\text{m s}^{-1}$.
Which graph shows the variation of frequency $f$ with the wavelength $\lambda$ for the waves in the string and in the air?

A.alt: Graph of f against λ with both axes starting at 0, showing two straight lines through the origin, labelled air and string.

B.alt: Graph of f against λ with both axes starting at 0, showing two straight lines through the origin, labelled string and air.

C.alt: Graph of f against λ with both axes starting at 0, showing two decreasing curves, labelled string and air.

D.alt: Graph of f against λ with both axes starting at 0, showing two decreasing curves, labelled air and string.
